Every quote to replace my oak cabinets started at $5,000. The actual fix was an $89 kit and a trip to the paint counter for a custom tint. Full breakdown of what that really costs.

The burnt-orange cabinets all over Pinterest this week don't come out of the box that color. The $89 kit ships in 5 fixed colors — none of them orange. Here's how people are actually getting the tone.
An $89 cabinet kit sounds like a weekend project. Budget two kits ($180) and up to 3 weeks of cure time instead. Here's the realistic timeline reviewers actually reported.
Cabinet replacement: $5,000-$20,000. Refacing: $4,000-$10,000. An $89 paint kit: roughly 1-2% of either, if your cabinets are structurally sound and just dated.
The detail that makes repainted cabinets look like a real renovation instead of a paint job: $26.99 worth of matte black hardware, swapped while the doors are already off the hinges.
Cabinet paint cure takes up to 3 weeks. During that window the cabinet interiors are already fully emptied — which makes it the cheapest possible time to finally fix the corner cabinet.
A 30-pack of matte black cabinet pulls holds 4.7 stars across 38,159 ratings at $26.99. That's a big enough sample to trust the screw spacing lines up without redrilling.
Reviewers who've used the $89 cabinet kit on oak all mention the same three things: real ventilation for the deglosser smell, thin coats not thick ones, and cure time longer than the label suggests.
$24.99 buys 4 non-skid lazy susan turntables with a 4.7-star rating across 6,190 reviews. No installation — they just sit on the shelf while the cabinets are already emptied for paint cure.
New cabinet color, same decade-old dish towels: that contrast makes the rest of the kitchen look more dated, not less. $20 in plain cotton towels is the detail that finishes the room.
